lesenParts.text:
We talked to sixteen-year-old runner Maya Lin about her life on and off the track. Maya recently won the national junior 800-metre championship, but she remains surprisingly down-to-earth.

Interviewer: Maya, congratulations on your gold medal! How did you first get into running?
Maya: Thanks! Actually, it was by accident. When I was eleven, my school's running team was short of one person for a relay race. The coach saw me running to catch the school bus and asked me to fill in. I didn't even have proper running shoes! I ended up running really fast, and the coach suggested I join the club. Before that, I preferred playing video games and reading. I never imagined I would become an athlete.

Interviewer: How do you manage to balance your training with your schoolwork?
Maya: It isn't easy. I train for about two hours every day after school, and more on weekends. I have to be very organised. I do my homework on the bus or during lunch breaks. My friends are very understanding, though they sometimes complain that I can't hang out with them on Friday nights because I have to sleep early for Saturday morning practice. But they always come to support me at my races, which means a lot.

Interviewer: Do you ever feel too much pressure before a big race?
Maya: Definitely. Before a race, my hands shake and I feel sick. But my coach taught me to view that nervous energy as a positive thing. She says it shows my body is preparing to run fast. Once the race starts, all the worry disappears and I just focus on my breathing and my steps. I don't think about winning; I just try to beat my own personal best time.

Interviewer: What are your goals for the future?
Maya: Of course, the Olympics is the ultimate dream, but that is a long way off. For now, I want to focus on my next race and keep improving. I also want to finish my school exams with good grades because education is important to me. If I have one piece of advice for other young people, it's to try new things. You might discover a talent you never knew you had!

questions.explanation: Maya explains that her coach saw her running to catch the school bus and asked her to fill in for a relay race because they were short of one person.
options: a) She wanted to get fit instead of playing video games.

questions.explanation: Maya says her coach taught her to view nervous energy as a positive thing, showing that her body is preparing to run fast.
options: a) It makes her perform worse than she should.

c) She tries to ignore it by thinking about winning.
d) It is something she only felt when she was younger.

questions.question: What is Maya's main priority for the near future?

options: a) Making sure she does well in both her sport and her studies
b) Finding a new coach to help her improve her times
c) Qualifying for the next Olympic Games
d) Encouraging other teenagers to take up running

questions.explanation: At the end of the text, Maya advises other young people to try new things because they might discover a talent they never knew they had, which matches option c.
options: a) "I'm so lucky my school coach forced me to run. Without her, I would still be playing video games all day."
b) "It's tough when you have to give up all your hobbies and friends for a gold medal, but it's worth it in the end!"
c) "Never be afraid to step out of your comfort zone. You might find a passion you didn't know existed, just like I did!"
d) "If you want to be a champion, you must ignore the pressure and only focus on beating the other runners."

lesenParts.textTitle: A Weekend at the Local Food Market
lesenParts.text:
Last Saturday, I decided to visit the local food market in the town centre. I had heard a lot about it from my neighbours, but I had never found the time to go before. [1] As soon as I arrived, I realised I should have come much sooner. The atmosphere was incredibly lively and full of energy.

There were dozens of colourful stalls selling everything from fresh fruit to homemade cakes. [2] The smell of freshly baked bread was particularly amazing, drawing a huge crowd to one corner. I spent about an hour just walking around and looking at all the delicious options.

What I liked most was talking to the people who worked there. [3] They were happy to explain how they made their cheese or where their vegetables were grown. This made the shopping experience feel much more personal than going to a normal supermarket.

By lunchtime, I was starting to feel quite hungry because of all the wonderful smells. [4] I chose a small stall selling traditional Spanish empanadas and sat on a wooden bench to eat them. They were absolutely delicious and very filling.

Before leaving, I bought some fresh pasta and a jar of local honey to take home. [5] I am already planning my next visit and cannot wait to try some of the other stalls.

lesenParts.text: Last July, my friends and I decided to (1) ______ the Green Valley Music Festival. It is one of the most popular outdoor events in the country, and it (2) ______ place every summer in a beautiful forest. We arrived early on Friday morning to set up our tent in the camping area. As soon as the music started, the atmosphere became absolutely (3) ______. There were several stages with different types of music, so there was always something great to listen to. We spent most of our time dancing and eating delicious local food from the stalls. Although it (4) ______ with rain on Saturday night, nobody seemed to mind. We just put on our raincoats and kept on singing. The organisers also handed out free hot drinks to everyone. It was an unforgettable weekend, and we have already (5) ______ to buy our tickets for next year. I would highly (6) ______ this festival to anyone who loves live music and nature.

questions.question: Choose the correct word for gap (1).
questions.explanation: 'Attend' is the correct verb to use when you go to an event like a festival, concert, or meeting. 'Assist' means to help, which does not fit the context.
options: a) invite
b) attend
c) assist
d) present

questions.question: Choose the correct word for gap (2).
questions.explanation: 'Takes place' is a common collocation meaning to happen or occur in a particular place.
options: a) gives

questions.explanation: 'Amazing' fits perfectly to describe an exciting and positive atmosphere. 'Pleased' and 'satisfied' describe how people feel, not the atmosphere itself.

options: a) encourage

lesenParts.textTitle: A Family Trip to the Mountains
lesenParts.text:
Last weekend, my family and I went on a trip to the mountains. We decided to go [1] car because it was easier to carry all our bags. The journey took about three hours, and [2] the weather was a bit cloudy at first, it soon became sunny.

When we arrived, we stayed in a lovely wooden cabin [3] was located next to a beautiful lake. My father immediately suggested going for a walk. We walked [4] hours along the forest paths. We even saw some wild deer! Later, my younger brother and I spent the afternoon swimming in the cold, clear water of the lake.

In the evening, we cooked a delicious meal together. Then we all sat outside and looked at the thousands of bright stars above the quiet valley. It was [5] a wonderful experience that we have already decided to return next year. I am really looking forward [6] our next adventure in the mountains.

questions.question: Identify the missing word for gap [1].
questions.explanation: We use the preposition 'by' to talk about means of transport (by car, by train, by bus).

questions.question: Identify the missing word for gap [2].
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'although' (or 'though') is used to introduce a contrast between the cloudy weather and it becoming sunny.

questions.question: Identify the missing word for gap [3].
questions.explanation: We use the relative pronoun 'which' (or 'that') to refer back to a thing (the wooden cabin) in a relative clause.

questions.question: Identify the missing word for gap [4].
questions.explanation: The preposition 'for' is used to show a period of time (for hours).

questions.question: Identify the missing word for gap [5].
questions.explanation: We use 'such' before 'a/an + adjective + singular noun' to add emphasis to the statement.

questions.question: Identify the missing word for gap [6].
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'look forward to' always takes the preposition 'to' followed by a noun, pronoun, or gerund.

[Woman]: Did you go to the indoor climbing wall yesterday, Jack?
[Man]: I wanted to, but it was fully booked. My brother suggested going for a bike ride instead, but then his bicycle had a flat tire. So we ended up playing tennis at the local club.
[Woman]: At least you did some exercise!

[Man]: I need to get a birthday present for my sister. I was thinking of a silver necklace.
[Woman]: She doesn't really wear jewellery, does she? What about that book she wanted?
[Man]: Our parents already bought her that. I think I'll get her a nice wool scarf instead. It's getting cold now.
[Woman]: That's a lovely idea.

[Man]: I can't find my keys anywhere! I thought I left them on the kitchen table next to my wallet.
[Woman]: Did you check your coat pocket? You had them when we came inside.
[Man]: Yes, I checked. Oh, wait, I remember now. I put them down on the shelf by the front door when I was taking off my shoes.
[Woman]: Ah, yes, there they are!

[Woman]: Look at my new bag! I wanted a small round one, but when I got to the shop, I saw this square leather one and fell in love with it.
[Man]: It's nice. I thought you were looking for one with long straps to wear over your shoulder?
[Woman]: I was, but this one has short handles and it's actually much easier to carry.

[Man]: Hi Sarah, are we still meeting at quarter past five?
[Woman]: Well, my class doesn't finish until five o'clock, and it takes me half an hour to get to the café. Can we make it quarter to six instead?
[Man]: That's a bit late because the film starts at six. Let's say half past five.
[Woman]: Okay, see you then.

[Man]: Shall we go to that new Italian restaurant by the river for lunch?
[Woman]: I'd love to, but it's always so busy. Why don't we just get some sandwiches and sit in the park? It's really sunny today.
[Man]: Actually, I heard there's a lovely café inside the museum that has outdoor seating. It's quiet too.
[Woman]: Oh, that sounds perfect. Let's go there.

[Presenter]: Here is the weather forecast for tomorrow. It will be a very wet start to the day, with heavy rain during the morning. However, by lunchtime, the rain will clear up, leaving us with cloudy but dry skies for the rest of the afternoon. We might even see some sunshine by the evening.

Boy: I'd love to, but my boots are completely worn out. I need to buy a new pair before I do any serious climbing.
Girl: You could always borrow my brother's. He's got some spares.
Boy: Thanks, but hiking boots need to fit perfectly, otherwise you get terrible blisters. I'll just go shopping on Saturday instead.

questions.question: You hear two friends talking about a weekend hike. Why is the boy unable to go?
questions.explanation: The boy says his boots are worn out and he cannot borrow a pair because they must fit perfectly to avoid blisters, meaning he lacks the correct footwear.
options: a) He has to go shopping for clothes.
b) He doesn't have the right footwear.
c) He has to help his brother.

segments.label: Recording 5
segments.transcript:
Boy: Did you see the photos I took at the park yesterday?
Girl: Yes, they're really good! The lighting on the lake was perfect. But why didn't you get closer to the birds? They look a bit small.
Boy: I know, but I didn't want to scare them away. Next time I'll use a better zoom lens.
Girl: Good idea. Still, you've got a real talent for finding great angles.

questions.question: You hear two friends talking about photography. What does the girl think the boy should improve?
questions.explanation: The girl points out that the birds in the photos look a bit small and asks why he didn't get closer, which refers to the size of the subjects in his shots.
options: a) The angles he chooses to shoot from
b) The lighting in his photos
c) The size of the subjects in his shots

segments.label: Recording 6
segments.transcript:
Man: I'm thinking of giving up the guitar. I've been practicing for three months and I still can't play a whole song.
Woman: Don't be so hard on yourself! It takes time. Are you practicing every day?
Man: Well, only on weekends, really. I'm too tired after work.
Woman: That's the problem. Even fifteen minutes a day during the week would make a huge difference.

questions.question: You hear a woman talking to a friend who is learning the guitar. What is she doing?
questions.explanation: The woman suggests that practicing for fifteen minutes a day during the week, rather than only on weekends, would make a huge difference, which is proposing a better routine.
options: a) Agreeing that learning the guitar is too difficult
b) Suggesting a more effective practice routine
c) Recommending a different instrument to try

horenParts.instruction: Listen and answer the questions in Part 3.
horenParts.transcript:
Hello everyone, and thank you for joining our tour group today. I want to give you some practical information about our visit to the Science Museum tomorrow.

First, we will meet outside the main entrance at 8.45 am. Please don't be late as the bus leaves at exactly nine o'clock.

When we arrive, we will start our visit in the transport gallery on the ground floor. This is always very popular because of the old steam trains.

After that, you will have some free time. I highly recommend visiting the special exhibition on the first floor. It is about robots and how they are used in everyday life.

For lunch, you can eat your own sandwiches in the picnic area, which is next to the museum shop. Please do not eat inside the exhibition rooms.

In the afternoon, we have booked a special 3D film in the IMAX cinema. The film is about the history of space exploration. It starts at two-thirty and lasts for forty minutes.

Finally, before we go home, you can visit the gift shop. If you show your group ticket, you can get a discount on books and posters.

Are there any questions?

horenParts.instruction: Listen and answer the questions in Part 4.
horenParts.transcript:
Interviewer: Today I'm talking to Elena Rossi, a successful travel blogger. Elena, welcome. Why did you first start your blog, 'Elena's Footsteps'?

Elena: Well, I didn't plan to make it my job! I actually started it when I went on a gap year to South America. My parents were really worried, so I promised to write regular updates so they'd know I was safe. I didn't think anyone else would read it, but then other travellers started finding my posts and asking for advice.

Interviewer: That's amazing. You've been to so many countries. Which one stands out the most?

Elena: People always ask this! I love Japan for its food, and Iceland for the landscapes, but my absolute favourite was Albania. I didn't know much about it before going, but the local people were incredibly welcoming. One family even invited me into their home for dinner when I got lost. That kindness is what I remember most.

Interviewer: Travelling isn't always easy, though. How do you deal with things when they go wrong?

Elena: Oh, I've had missed flights, lost luggage, and food poisoning! At first, I used to get really stressed and angry. But I quickly realised that doesn't help. Now, I just accept that problems are part of the adventure. I try to stay calm and look for a solution, often by asking locals. They are usually happy to help a confused tourist.

Interviewer: You usually travel by yourself. Do you prefer that?

Elena: I do. When you travel with friends, you tend to stay in your own little bubble. But when you're on your own, you're forced to talk to strangers, which means you make new friends much faster. Of course, it can be lonely occasionally, but the freedom to decide where to go next without arguing is worth it.

Interviewer: What's the most challenging part of being a professional blogger?

Elena: People think it's a permanent holiday, but it's hard work. The toughest thing for me is the lack of a routine. I'm constantly moving, which makes it hard to exercise regularly or eat healthily. I don't mind the long hours spent editing photos or writing posts, because I love doing that, but not having a proper home base can be exhausting.

Interviewer: Finally, what tips do you have for someone wanting to start a travel blog?

Elena: Don't just write about the famous tourist spots that everyone knows. Try to find a unique angle. Write about your personal feelings and the small details, like the smell of a local market. And most importantly, write because you love it, not because you want to get free hotel rooms. Readers can tell if you aren't being genuine.

Interviewer: Thank you, Elena!

schreibenParts.task:
Read this email from your English-speaking friend Alex and the notes you have made.

***
From: Alex
Subject: Your new course!

Hi,

How are you? I heard you started a new course last week. What kind of course is it? [Tell Alex]

I'd love to know if you are enjoying it. Is the teacher nice? [Great!]

Maybe I can join you next time. When is the next class? [Answer]

Let's meet up this weekend to talk about it. Which day is better for you? [Suggest]

Write back soon,
Alex
***

Write your email to Alex using all the notes. You should write about 100 words.

Choose one of the following tasks (article or story). Write about 100 words.

Option 1: Article
You see this notice on an international English website for young people:

*Articles wanted!*
LEARNING SOMETHING NEW
What is a new skill you would like to learn? Why do you want to learn it? Is it easy or difficult for young people to learn new things?
Write an article answering these questions.

OR

Option 2: Story
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence:

*It was my first day at the class.*
Write your story.

sprechenParts.title: Part 1 — Speaking
sprechenParts.situation:
Phase 1:
What is your name?
Where do you live?
Do you work or are you a student?

Phase 2 (Topic: Free time and daily routine):
What do you usually do in your free time?
Do you prefer spending your free time alone or with friends? Why?
Tell us about your daily routine on weekdays.
What is your favourite part of the day? Why?

sprechenParts.title: Part 2 — Speaking
sprechenParts.situation:
Describe this photo: A colour photo of people relaxing in a park.

Talk about what you can see in the picture (the people, their clothes, the weather, the activities, and the background) for about 1 minute.

sprechenParts.title: Part 3 — Speaking
sprechenParts.situation:
A group of friends has a free Saturday afternoon together in town. Talk together about the different things they could do, and decide which would be the best option.

Here are some ideas:
Going to the cinema
Having a picnic in the park
Visiting a local museum
Going shopping
Playing board games at a café

Discuss these options with your partner and agree on the best activity.

sprechenParts.title: Part 4 — Speaking
sprechenParts.situation:
Discuss these questions with your partner:
Do you prefer active free-time activities (like sports) or relaxing ones (like reading)? Why?
How much free time do you think people should have every day?
Is it important to try new hobbies, or is it better to stick to the ones you know?
Do you think people spend too much time on their phones during their free time nowadays?
